subject: Re: remediation tranches, escrowed cash collar, and stepdown termination proposal
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@x-corp.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@x-corp.com
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed remedies: cash-collar and stepdown termination staircase

Hiro / Ben,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Procurement has pushed back on the standard credits-only approach — their risk policy requires a tangible fee-at-risk construct for core infrastructure providers. Attached is a short redline that outlines what they want:

- Escrowed cash collar equal to 3 months of committed fees, released to X Corp if the service misses aggregated uptime targets for two consecutive months.
- A "stepdown termination" right: if severity-1 incidents exceed 4 in a rolling 90-day window and remediation milestones are missed twice, X Corp can terminate for convenience with a 60-day notice and receive the escrowed collar plus a capped liquidated damages payment (1 month revenue).
- For single-month outages we still prefer credits, but procurement wants a clear path to cash when degradation is persistent.

I know this is outside standard Redwood commercial language. Please confirm whether you can accept the escrow + staged termination ladder or if you need alternative guardrails. If helpful, procurement is available for a brief call to explain their risk model.

Attachment: XCorp_Remedy_Redline_20280910.pdf

Best,
Elena Morris
Director of Procurement
X Corporation
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@x-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed remedies: cash-collar and stepdown termination staircase

Elena —

Thanks for sending the redline and the clear framing. I appreciate procurement's perspective; I want to be explicit about two constraints up front: legal caps on liability and our standard cure windows. That said, we are open to structured exceptions for strategic customers. High level reaction:

- Escrowed collar: possible in principle but would need to be limited (we typically cap cash at-risk to a multiple of monthly recurring revenue and require a concrete remediation plan tied to releases).
- Stepdown termination: we can consider a staged termination right but would prefer a cure ladder (60 days cure + operational remediation plan) before cash transfers.
- Liquidated damages: Redwood typically avoids open-ended LD clauses; if a cash remedy is required we propose a capped, per-incident schedule and an aggregate cap.

Next steps: Ben (sales) and I will sync with legal and finance tomorrow and come back with a counterproposal that preserves a path to cash but limits our exposure and ties payouts to remediation milestones. Can procurement do a 30-minute call on Tuesday (any time after 10am PT)?

— Hiro Tanaka
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@x-corp.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed remedies: cash-collar and stepdown termination staircase

Elena — quick note from our side: procurement's ask makes sense given your internal audit. Couple of practical questions that will impact our counter:

1) Measurement: is procurement okay with using Redwood's platform-level uptime metric (minutes of availability across the customer-dedicated pool) rather than counting every customer-reported incident? We want to avoid conflicting incident logs.
2) Severity granularity: proposed threshold (4 SEV1s / 90 days) — can you share what counts today as a SEV1 for you? For example, would short bursts of latency that don't affect core transactions be in scope?

If measurement can be standardized we can consider a cash-collar staged release: hold 3 months in escrow, release funds only after (a) two consecutive months of failing aggregated uptime AND (b) failed remediation milestones within the agreed cure timetable. Otherwise, we should adjust the collar size downward.

I can join the Tuesday slot if you confirm.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@x-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@x-corp.com
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed remedies: cash-collar and stepdown termination staircase

Ben/Hiro —

Thanks, those clarifying Qs are helpful. Procurement prefers platform-level uptime as the canonical measurement but will require Redwood to publish the aggregated monthly uptime calculation and provide access to the incident log for 90-day windows. If you can limit the collar to an escrowed amount, procurement is flexible on the exact release mechanics as long as the money is available on a short timetable (10 business days) after the failure conditions are met.

On severity: for X Corp a SEV1 is defined as a customer-impacting outage that prevents core API transactions for >2 minutes. Brief latency spikes that do not cause transaction failure are not counted.

Procurement also emphasized they will need an option to terminate without cause after the second missed remediation milestone in a 180-day period (this is the stepdown they want). They are willing to accept a commercially reasonable cure window, but they cannot accept credits alone as the sole remedy for repeated degradations.

We have a calendar hold at 10:30am PT Tuesday for the call.

Best,
Elena
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed remedies: cash-collar and stepdown termination staircase — request for exception approval

Marissa — forwarding the thread and the redline. X Corp (strategic target, XD-4572) is asking for an escrowed cash collar (3 months' committed fees) plus a stepdown termination right tied to repeated SEV1s and missed remediation milestones. Procurement insists credits-only is insufficient.

We should decide whether to:
1) Offer a limited-cash collar (escrow capped at 2 months MRC), explicit remediation milestones, and an aggregate liability cap at 3x MRC with a per-incident cap; OR
2) Maintain credits-only in the public SaaS T&C and offer the full escrow + stepdown only via a one-time addendum that requires finance/legal sign-off and a 25% pricing uplift to offset risk.

Legal/Finance concerns:
- Precedent for escrowed cash at scale across dedicated pools.
- Accounting treatment and revenue recognition impact.
- Need for a clear measurement/telemetry artifact we control (or a mutually-agreed third-party metric).

Attached: XCorp_Remedy_Redline_20280910.pdf

Can you weigh in ASAP? Procurement is on a tight schedule. If we go with option 2 we should prepare the addendum and pricing delta before tomorrow's call.

— Hiro
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
